#region zsh
$ agx shell-init --shell zsh
# agx shell layer (zsh), generated by `agx shell-init --shell zsh`.
# Load it with: eval "$(agx shell-init --shell zsh)". Edit the config, not this output.
\builtin export AGX_SHELL=zsh

# The definitions below are parsed with your aliases switched off, then the
# setting is restored: the layer is eval'd in your shell, where an alias such
# as `alias do='cd ~/Downloads'` or `alias then=...` would break its parse (and
# with it every function) and `alias cd=...` would run instead of cd. zsh
# parses a whole eval at once, so the definitions are one quoted eval run
# after the switch. Your aliases still work everywhere else, and one named
# like a function here still wins when you type it.
__agx_aliases=${options[aliases]}
\builtin unsetopt aliases
\builtin eval '
# __agx_has FLAG ARGS...: whether ARGS hold FLAG or FLAG=... before a bare
# --. It recurses instead of looping, so the layer has no for/do/done at all.
__agx_has() {
  local __agx_f=$1
  shift
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && return 1
  case "$1" in
    --) return 1 ;;
    "$__agx_f"|"$__agx_f"=*) return 0 ;;
  esac
  shift
  __agx_has "$__agx_f" "$@"
}

# agx: one wrapper around the binary for the two things a child process
# cannot do for its shell. `new` and `resume` write a plan, cd to its folder,
# then start the agent from it; `login ... --terminal` sets AGX_LOGIN here.
# Everything else goes straight to the binary.
agx() {
  case "$1" in
    new|resume)
      local __agx_cmd __agx_plan __agx_dir __agx_rc
      __agx_cmd=$1
      shift
      __agx_plan=$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agx-plan.XXXXXX") || return 125
      command agx "$__agx_cmd" --plan-file "$__agx_plan" "$@"
      __agx_rc=$?
      if [ "$__agx_rc" -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$__agx_plan" ]; then
        command rm -f -- "$__agx_plan"
        return "$__agx_rc"
      fi
      __agx_dir=$(command agx plan show --plan-file "$__agx_plan" --field data.dir) &&
        builtin cd -- "$__agx_dir" || {
        command rm -f -- "$__agx_plan"
        return 125
      }
      command agx launch --plan-file "$__agx_plan"
      __agx_rc=$?
      command rm -f -- "$__agx_plan"
      return "$__agx_rc"
      ;;
    login)
      local __agx_out __agx_rc
      if __agx_has --terminal "$@"; then
        __agx_out=$(command agx "$@")
        __agx_rc=$?
        case "$__agx_out" in
          "export AGX_LOGIN="*)
            export AGX_LOGIN="${__agx_out#"export AGX_LOGIN="}"
            builtin printf "%s\n" "agx: AGX_LOGIN=$AGX_LOGIN in this shell" >&2
            ;;
          "unset AGX_LOGIN")
            unset AGX_LOGIN
            builtin printf "%s\n" "agx: AGX_LOGIN unset in this shell" >&2
            ;;
          *)
            [ -n "$__agx_out" ] && builtin printf "%s\n" "$__agx_out"
            ;;
        esac
        return "$__agx_rc"
      fi
      command agx "$@"
      ;;
    *)
      command agx "$@"
      ;;
  esac
}
#region zsh-aliases
cl() { agx run --profile personal "$@"; }
clw() { agx run --profile work "$@"; }
#endregion zsh-aliases

'
\builtin test "$__agx_aliases" = on && \builtin setopt aliases
\builtin unset __agx_aliases

#endregion
#region bash
$ agx shell-init --shell bash
# agx shell layer (bash), generated by `agx shell-init --shell bash`.
# Load it with: eval "$(agx shell-init --shell bash)". Edit the config, not this output.
\builtin export AGX_SHELL=bash

# The definitions below are parsed with your aliases switched off, then the
# setting is restored: the layer is eval'd in your shell, where an alias such
# as `alias do='cd ~/Downloads'` or `alias then=...` would break its parse (and
# with it every function) and `alias cd=...` would run instead of cd. zsh
# parses a whole eval at once, so the definitions are one quoted eval run
# after the switch. Your aliases still work everywhere else, and one named
# like a function here still wins when you type it.
__agx_aliases=$(\builtin shopt -p expand_aliases)
\builtin shopt -u expand_aliases
\builtin eval '
# __agx_has FLAG ARGS...: whether ARGS hold FLAG or FLAG=... before a bare
# --. It recurses instead of looping, so the layer has no for/do/done at all.
__agx_has() {
  local __agx_f=$1
  shift
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && return 1
  case "$1" in
    --) return 1 ;;
    "$__agx_f"|"$__agx_f"=*) return 0 ;;
  esac
  shift
  __agx_has "$__agx_f" "$@"
}

# agx: one wrapper around the binary for the two things a child process
# cannot do for its shell. `new` and `resume` write a plan, cd to its folder,
# then start the agent from it; `login ... --terminal` sets AGX_LOGIN here.
# Everything else goes straight to the binary.
agx() {
  case "$1" in
    new|resume)
      local __agx_cmd __agx_plan __agx_dir __agx_rc
      __agx_cmd=$1
      shift
      __agx_plan=$(command mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/agx-plan.XXXXXX") || return 125
      command agx "$__agx_cmd" --plan-file "$__agx_plan" "$@"
      __agx_rc=$?
      if [ "$__agx_rc" -ne 0 ] || [ ! -s "$__agx_plan" ]; then
        command rm -f -- "$__agx_plan"
        return "$__agx_rc"
      fi
      __agx_dir=$(command agx plan show --plan-file "$__agx_plan" --field data.dir) &&
        builtin cd -- "$__agx_dir" || {
        command rm -f -- "$__agx_plan"
        return 125
      }
      command agx launch --plan-file "$__agx_plan"
      __agx_rc=$?
      command rm -f -- "$__agx_plan"
      return "$__agx_rc"
      ;;
    login)
      local __agx_out __agx_rc
      if __agx_has --terminal "$@"; then
        __agx_out=$(command agx "$@")
        __agx_rc=$?
        case "$__agx_out" in
          "export AGX_LOGIN="*)
            export AGX_LOGIN="${__agx_out#"export AGX_LOGIN="}"
            builtin printf "%s\n" "agx: AGX_LOGIN=$AGX_LOGIN in this shell" >&2
            ;;
          "unset AGX_LOGIN")
            unset AGX_LOGIN
            builtin printf "%s\n" "agx: AGX_LOGIN unset in this shell" >&2
            ;;
          *)
            [ -n "$__agx_out" ] && builtin printf "%s\n" "$__agx_out"
            ;;
        esac
        return "$__agx_rc"
      fi
      command agx "$@"
      ;;
    *)
      command agx "$@"
      ;;
  esac
}
cl() { agx run --profile personal "$@"; }
clw() { agx run --profile work "$@"; }

'
\builtin eval "$__agx_aliases"
\builtin unset __agx_aliases

#endregion
#region fish
$ agx shell-init --shell fish
# agx shell layer (fish), generated by `agx shell-init --shell fish`.
# Load it with: agx shell-init --shell fish | source. Edit the config, not this output.
set -gx AGX_SHELL fish

# agx: one wrapper around the binary for the two things a child process
# cannot do for its shell. `new` and `resume` write a plan, cd to its folder,
# then start the agent from it; `login ... --terminal` sets AGX_LOGIN here.
# Everything else goes straight to the binary. It calls builtin and command
# forms (builtin cd, builtin printf, command rm), so a function of yours with
# one of those names is never run in their place.
function agx --wraps agx --description 'agx shell layer'
    switch "$argv[1]"
        case new resume
            set -l tmp /tmp
            set -q TMPDIR; and set tmp $TMPDIR
            set -l plan (command mktemp "$tmp/agx-plan.XXXXXX"); or return 125
            command agx $argv[1] --plan-file $plan $argv[2..-1]
            set -l rc $status
            if test $rc -ne 0; or not test -s $plan
                command rm -f -- $plan
                return $rc
            end
            set -l dir (command agx plan show --plan-file $plan --field data.dir); and builtin cd $dir
            or begin
                command rm -f -- $plan
                return 125
            end
            command agx launch --plan-file $plan
            set rc $status
            command rm -f -- $plan
            return $rc
        case login
            if contains -- --terminal $argv
                set -l out (command agx $argv)
                set -l rc $status
                if test (count $out) -eq 1; and string match -q -- 'export AGX_LOGIN=*' $out[1]
                    set -gx AGX_LOGIN (string replace -- 'export AGX_LOGIN=' '' $out[1])
                    builtin printf '%s\n' "agx: AGX_LOGIN=$AGX_LOGIN in this shell" >&2
                else if test (count $out) -eq 1; and test "$out[1]" = 'unset AGX_LOGIN'
                    set -e AGX_LOGIN
                    builtin printf '%s\n' "agx: AGX_LOGIN unset in this shell" >&2
                else if test (count $out) -gt 0
                    builtin printf '%s\n' $out
                end
                return $rc
            end
            command agx $argv
        case '*'
            command agx $argv
    end
end
#region fish-aliases
function cl --wraps 'agx run --profile personal'
    agx run --profile personal $argv
end
function clw --wraps 'agx run --profile work'
    agx run --profile work $argv
end
#endregion fish-aliases

#endregion
#region pwsh
$ agx shell-init --shell pwsh
# agx shell layer (pwsh), generated by `agx shell-init --shell pwsh`.
# Load it with: agx shell-init --shell pwsh | Out-String | Invoke-Expression. Edit the config, not this output.
$env:AGX_SHELL = 'pwsh'

# agx: one wrapper around the binary for the two things a child process
# cannot do for its shell. `new` and `resume` write a plan, cd to its folder,
# then start the agent from it; `login ... --terminal` sets AGX_LOGIN here.
# Everything else goes straight to the binary.
# Cmdlets are called by their module-qualified names, so an alias or function
# of yours named Set-Location, Remove-Item or the like is never run instead.
#region pwsh-raw-args
# PowerShell consumes a bare -- when calling a function: quote it ('--') to
# pass arguments through to the agent.
#endregion pwsh-raw-args
function agx {
    $bin = (Microsoft.PowerShell.Core\Get-Command -Name 'agx' -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Stop | Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility\Select-Object -First 1).Source
    $rest = @($args | Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility\Select-Object -Skip 1)
    if ($args.Count -gt 0 -and @('new', 'resume') -contains $args[0]) {
        $plan = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName()
        & $bin $args[0] --plan-file $plan @rest
        $rc = $LASTEXITCODE
        if ($rc -ne 0 -or (Microsoft.PowerShell.Management\Get-Item -LiteralPath $plan).Length -eq 0) {
            Microsoft.PowerShell.Management\Remove-Item -Force -LiteralPath $plan
            $global:LASTEXITCODE = $rc
            return
        }
        $dir = & $bin plan show --plan-file $plan --field data.dir
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            Microsoft.PowerShell.Management\Remove-Item -Force -LiteralPath $plan
            $global:LASTEXITCODE = 125
            return
        }
        Microsoft.PowerShell.Management\Set-Location -LiteralPath $dir
        & $bin launch --plan-file $plan
        $rc = $LASTEXITCODE
        Microsoft.PowerShell.Management\Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -LiteralPath $plan
        $global:LASTEXITCODE = $rc
        return
    }
    if ($args.Count -gt 0 -and $args[0] -eq 'login' -and $args -contains '--terminal') {
        $out = @(& $bin @args)
        $rc = $LASTEXITCODE
        if ($out.Count -eq 1 -and $out[0].StartsWith('export AGX_LOGIN=')) {
            $env:AGX_LOGIN = $out[0].Substring('export AGX_LOGIN='.Length)
            [Console]::Error.WriteLine("agx: AGX_LOGIN=$env:AGX_LOGIN in this shell")
        } elseif ($out.Count -eq 1 -and $out[0] -eq 'unset AGX_LOGIN') {
            Microsoft.PowerShell.Management\Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue Env:AGX_LOGIN
            [Console]::Error.WriteLine("agx: AGX_LOGIN unset in this shell")
        } else {
            $out
        }
        $global:LASTEXITCODE = $rc
        return
    }
    & $bin @args
}
#region pwsh-aliases
function cl { agx run --profile personal @args }
function clw { agx run --profile work @args }
#endregion pwsh-aliases

#endregion
